props.title: Future War

sections.content: **Future War** (1997) stands as one of the most infamously inept direct-to-video sci-fi films, joining the pantheon of "so-bad-it's-good" classics like **Troll 2** (1990) and **The Room** (2003). Despite its futuristic title, the film bizarrely features dinosaurs chasing a cyborg through contemporary Los Angeles warehouses. The budget constraints are painfully obvious - the dinosaurs are clearly toys filmed in close-up, and the "cyborg" appears to be wearing leftover Halloween costume parts.

sections.content: The film's production context reflects the 1990s direct-to-video boom, when companies like PM Entertainment and AIP churned out low-budget genre films to fill video store shelves. **Future War** emerged alongside countless knockoffs trying to capitalize on bigger hits like **Terminator 2: Judgment Day** (1991) and **Jurassic Park** (1993). The film's director, Anthony Doublin, only directed one other feature, exemplifying the "one-and-done" nature of many DTV filmmakers of the era.

What makes **Future War** particularly fascinating is its bizarre mixture of incompatible genre elements. While films like **Hardware** (1990) and **Death Machine** (1994) successfully blended cyber-horror with practical effects on low budgets, **Future War** throws logic out the window by combining cyborgs, dinosaurs, and martial arts without any coherent explanation. The lead actor, Daniel Bernhardt, was actually a kickboxer hired more for his fighting ability than acting skills - a common practice in 1990s DTV action films. SUBHEAD: The MST3K Effect

sections.content: **Future War** gained its greatest notoriety when featured on **Mystery Science Theater 3000** (1997), joining other memorable episodes featuring films like **Space Mutiny** (1988) and **Time Chasers** (1994). The MST3K treatment highlighted the film's countless continuity errors, visible boom mics, and cardboard box-heavy set design. This exposure transformed the film from obscure video store filler into a celebrated piece of sci-fi schlock.
